quality_guards: Lead risk depends on chemical form, concentration, task, dust or fume generation, exposure route, duration, controls and worker susceptibility.
Lead guidance is task-, material-, exposure- and worker-specific and is not an exact parcel-level illness probability.
Ionising-radiation risk depends on radiation type, activity or generator output, geometry, shielding, time, distance, containment and emergency conditions.
Ionising-radiation evidence is source-, task-, dose-, facility- and person-specific and is not an exact parcel-level health probability.
Sharps risk depends on device design, contamination, procedure, handling, disposal access, training, patient factors and post-exposure response.
Sharps guidance is device-, procedure-, exposure- and person-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.
Cytotoxic-drug risk depends on drug, formulation, task, contamination, exposure route, frequency, scale, controls and worker susceptibility.
Cytotoxic evidence is drug-, task-, route-, worker- and incident-specific and is not an exact parcel-level health probability.
Surface-engineering risk depends on process chemistry, bath or coating type, temperature, machine energy, ventilation, access and maintenance.
Surface-engineering evidence is process-, chemical-, machine-, task- and worker-specific and is not an exact parcel-level incident probability.
Powder-coating risk depends on formulation, particle size, booth airflow, spraying method, transfer and cleaning tasks, maintenance and PPE.
Powder-coating evidence is product-, booth-, task-, exposure- and worker-specific and is not an exact parcel-level health probability.
Refrigeration risk depends on refrigerant, inventory, pressure, temperature, plant design, corrosion, ventilation, occupancy and emergency capability.
Refrigeration evidence is system-, refrigerant-, failure-mode-, location- and operating-condition-specific and is not an exact parcel-level accident probability.
Textile and laundry risk depends on fibre, chemical, contamination, process, ventilation, task duration, cleaning method and worker susceptibility.
Textile and laundry evidence is material-, process-, exposure- and worker-specific and is not an exact parcel-level respiratory-disease probability.
WEL interpretation depends on substance identity, sampling method, averaging period, exposure route, mixtures, task pattern and control reliability.
An air limit does not by itself determine individual dose, health outcome or an exact parcel-level probability.
Hairdressing risk depends on product chemistry, wet-work duration, ventilation, glove selection, aerosol generation, task and individual sensitisation.
Hairdressing evidence is product-, task-, exposure-, client- and worker-specific and is not an exact parcel-level asthma or dermatitis probability.
Official-source context is not converted into an exact parcel-level probability.
